topic.subject: science
topic.title: Motion
topic.scope: distance vs displacement, speed vs velocity, acceleration, uniform circular motion, graphs, equations of motion

misconceptions.statement: Distance and displacement are always the same thing.
misconceptions.why: In daily life, we use the terms interchangeably when describing travel between two points.
misconceptions.fix: Distance is the total path length covered, while displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the starting point to the finish.

probe.question: If a runner completes one full lap around a 400m circular track, what is their displacement?

misconceptions.statement: An object moving at a constant speed must have a constant velocity.
misconceptions.why: Students often ignore the directional component of velocity, focusing only on the magnitude.
misconceptions.fix: Velocity includes both speed and direction; if the direction changes, the velocity changes even if the speed remains constant.

probe.question: A car turns a corner at a steady 20 km/h. Does its velocity change?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because the speed is constant.

misconceptions.statement: If an object is moving, it must have acceleration.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the state of 'being in motion' with the state of 'changing motion'.
misconceptions.fix: Acceleration only occurs when there is a change in velocity over time; an object moving at a steady speed in a straight line has zero acceleration.

probe.question: A train is moving at a constant 80 km/h in a straight line. What is its acceleration?
probe.wrong_answer: It is high because the train is moving fast.

misconceptions.statement: The slope of a distance-time graph represents the acceleration of the object.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate the visual steepness of a graph with the concept of 'getting faster'.
misconceptions.fix: The slope of a distance-time graph represents speed; the slope of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration.

probe.question: On a distance-time graph, what does a straight line sloping upwards indicate?
